title: Elkik pairs, finite unions, and the regular functoriality hypothesis
statement: An affine Elkik pair consists of a commutative ring $A$, a characteristic-zero field $k$, a finite-type structure morphism $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $\pi\in A$ a non-zero-divisor such that every nonregular point lies in $V(\pi)$ [def-weil-regular-scheme]. An Elkik union is a scheme $X$ with quasi-coherent ideal $I$ admitting a finite disjoint-union presentation by such affine pairs, with $I$ extending to each principal ideal; the empty union and different fields on the pieces are allowed. Its thick fibre is $V(I^t)$ with distinguished ideal $I\mathcal O_{V(I^t)}$, and its completed formal ringed space is that of [def-per-adic-formal-geometry], using the scheme-ideal and formal-spectrum constructions of [def-per-rig-regular-formal-pair-geometry]. A variety union is a finite disjoint union of generically reduced finite-type schemes over characteristic-zero fields; generic reducedness is equivalently reducedness [def-pc-reduced-scheme] on a dense open in this Noetherian setting. An assignment $F$ of ordinary ordered towers [def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule] is strong regular-functorial on these variety unions if its centers are coherent [pqf-def-coherent], nonempty and regular, lie over the original nonregular locus, and its terminal scheme is regular, and every regular scheme morphism [def-per-regular-scheme-morphism] between variety unions gives the contracted cartesian tower comparison of [def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule], retaining exactly the nonempty extended ideals in order. No field-linearity is required. Values of the assignment outside variety unions are immaterial.
